Discoverable secondary subjects: an abandoned invading military tracked vehicle with a thrown track near the depot and a separate damaged military communications van with a folded antenna beside a shed. These are static scenery, neutral dark graphite/olive, no Ukrainian markings on them. No bodies or gore. One small recognizable Ukrainian FPV quadcopter in the foreground near a repair case: thin X-shaped carbon frame, four clearly separate three-bladed propellers, compact strapped battery, tiny front camera, restrained blue/yellow tape, not a large consumer camera drone. This is an original fictional illustration, not a documentary scene or a map of real positions. Avoid smooth painted gradients, 3D rendering, photorealistic textures, vector-flat shapes. Compose several rewarding discoveries across the width without centering a giant hero. Keep high-contrast tiny white and neon-pink cues sparse so live game actors remain legible on top. Dark navy shadows, muted olive and graphite machinery, wheat-gold dawn, restrained cool-blue accents. The atmosphere is resilient and hopeful with a strong 1980s/90s arcade cover-art feeling. No HUD, no grid, no live actors/enemy icons, no capture lines, no frame, no logos, no writing, no watermarks, no Z symbols anywhere. All terrain and vehicles are painted scenery; the game will supply actual collision and actors separately.
